clue.text: Given this, one must hit the right note — it's essential to get on

definitions.text: Given this, one must hit the right note

parts.note: a key thing is an essential or crucial one
to board a train or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: Advice that hitting the right note is essential to getting on in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: with a keyboard in front of you, you play notes by hitting keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument such as a piano produces each note when the player strikes the matching key.

clue.text: Passing things in record time across border (English)

indicators.note: the time comes across, on the far side of, the border, so it follows it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the border of a garment
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something passing through a record-breaking time across a national border, with English noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemerae are short-lived things, like mayflies, that pass away almost as soon as they appear.

clue.text: Most brave, better than all others, inwardly worn out?

indicators.note: inwardly asks for the next piece to go into the middle of the first

parts.note: the best is better than every rival
old things are worn out

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the bravest, who outdo everyone, are secretly exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold is a synonym of brave, so the superlative boldest is most brave.

clue.text: Casual notice — wine in short supply

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the final letter from the wine's name

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A notice that wine is running low at an informal gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc arrangements are improvised for the moment rather than planned, hence casual.

clue.text: European abandoning European tribe

indicators.note: abandoning tells us the second European, the abbreviation, is dropped from the first

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A European leaving behind his fellow Europeans and his tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel in the Bible.

clue.text: Only some of brigade armed? I'm shocked!

indicators.note: Only some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Surprise that only part of a brigade has been issued weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is an exclamation of dismay or surprise, the same reaction as saying one is shocked.

clue.text: Journey over valley, on reflection, made little sense

indicators.note: in a down entry the journey sits over, above, the next piece

parts.note: a drive is a journey by car

indicators.note: reflection as in a mirror means the valley word is read backwards

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: Someone thinking back on a drive through a valley and finding the talk was nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to talk silly nonsense, so drivelled means spoke without making sense.

clue.text: In that broadcast conflict comes across

indicators.note: In says the conflict word is placed within the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of that are scattered into a new order

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A report that conflict comes across in a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the clue word into ATHT, and 'In' signals the insertion; 'comes' is only a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart is an old preposition meaning from side to side, crosswise, that is across.

clue.text: Extracted material to be brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: denim is a cotton material

explanation.surface: Instructions that dug-out material should be carried up to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined describes coal or ore that has been dug out and so extracted from the ground.

clue.text: Bit of food in hospital eaten by boy, going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the whole assembly is read backwards
eaten by means the hospital letter goes inside the boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A boy in hospital swallowing a morsel that goes down the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is a lentil dish from South Asian cooking, an item of food.

clue.text: Joined two workers outside home

indicators.note: the workers stand outside, around, the home word

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand, so two workers are hand and hand
in means at home

explanation.surface: A pair of labourers joined together outside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in hand describes people linked by clasped hands, or things closely joined together.

clue.text: That Cockney fellow allowing a little kiss, it's said, being virtuous?

parts.note: him in Cockney speech drops the H to become 'im

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word is heard, not seen, so the spelling may change

parts.note: peckable means able to receive a peck, a little kiss

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Cockney man who allows quick kisses counts as virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: Peccable, from Latin peccare, means liable to sin, so its negative means sinless. The dropped H is the Cockney touch signalled by 'That Cockney fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeccable means incapable of sin or fault, so flawless and morally virtuous.

clue.text: Bewildered female escaped, having upset sailor earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the sailor part in front of the rest
upset in a down entry means turned upside down, read the other way

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
fled means escaped

explanation.surface: A woman confused after running away from a sailor she knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Baffled means puzzled or perplexed, a close synonym of bewildered.

clue.text: One helping girl to avoid extremes

indicators.note: extremes are the outer letters, which are dropped from the girl word

parts.note: a maiden is a girl

explanation.surface: A helper advising a young woman to steer clear of extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant, someone who helps another in their work.

clue.text: Forget about request by snail mail?

definitions.meaning: to ... a debt or loss is to forget about it as lost
to send a letter asking for it

explanation.surface: Dismissing the idea of asking for something by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Write off means both to cancel something as lost and to apply in writing by post.

clue.text: Refusal to get up — those folk stop getting better

indicators.note: get up in a down clue means the word rises, read from the bottom

parts.note: no is a refusal
them means those people
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to get out of bed while others stop recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness, gradually improving.

clue.text: Player of instrument shows excessive desire to hold note

indicators.note: to hold means the desire word contains the note

parts.note: lust is excessive desire
ti is the seventh note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A musician showing too much eagerness to sustain one note.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutist is a musician who plays the lute, a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Prim dean's turned into superhero

indicators.note: turned into means the letters are changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A prudish college dean transformed into a superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel comics hero with spider powers.

clue.text: This writer's wearing fur maybe — a frilly covering?

indicators.note: wearing means the writer is wrapped in the fur

parts.note: a pelt is an animal skin, fur for example
this writer is me, the setter; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: The setter wondering whether a fur garment counts as frilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelmet is a decorative strip, often ruffled, fitted above a window to hide the curtain fittings.

clue.text: Fellow has to squeeze inside clerical garment

indicators.note: inside puts the squeeze word within the fellow word

parts.note: a male is a fellow
to nip is to pinch or squeeze

explanation.surface: A man forced to squeeze into a priest's vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple is a strip of cloth worn on the left arm by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Boy terribly shy one in front of papa giving formal address

indicators.note: in front of puts the one before the papa letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of shy are badly jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
P is papa in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A very shy boy stepping ahead of his father to make a formal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Your Ladyship is the polite form used to speak to a titled woman.

clue.text: Look after that rising river with old form of technology

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means read upwards

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Watching over a rising river with outdated equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: See to it is an idiom meaning take care of a matter, make sure it is dealt with.

clue.text: Only half the local outlets offering healthy food?

indicators.note: only half asks for the first half of the outlet word

parts.note: branches are local outlets of a chain of shops or banks

explanation.surface: Only half of the neighbourhood shops selling health foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husks of cereal grain, is eaten as a fibre-rich health food.

clue.text: Loose dog maybe nipping the Parisian

indicators.note: nipping means the dog grips the French article between its letters

parts.note: Rex is a stock name for a dog
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A dog on the loose biting a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to loose and to relax both mean to slacken or loosen a grip.

clue.text: Finish filled with wrath — is put at risk

indicators.note: filled with means the finish word contains the wrath word

parts.note: ended means finished
anger is wrath

explanation.surface: An ending full of rage that puts someone in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' looks like a present-tense verb but stands for ENDED; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means placed in danger, threatened with harm.

clue.text: Smart part of America accommodating a Rechabite?

indicators.note: accommodating means the state abbreviation holds the following letters

parts.note: NY is New York, a state of the USA
the Rechabites are a temperance society, so a Rechabite is teetotal, TT

explanation.surface: Whether a stylish American state would put up a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty describes someone neatly and fashionably dressed, so smart in appearance.

clue.text: Tired as Bradman was on coming to the wicket for the last time?

definitions.text: as Bradman was on coming to the wicket for the last time
definitions.meaning: in his last Test innings in 1948 Don Bradman was applauded to the crease, clapped, and then bowled for nought, out

explanation.surface: Cricket history: the great batsman's farewell innings at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman, Australia's great batsman, needed four runs in his final Test to average 100, was cheered all the way to the crease and was out second ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out means worn out, exhausted, used of tired people or old machines.

clue.text: Grazing animal's heading off for grass

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a goat is a grazing animal; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A grazing animal heading out to graze on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grass grown for grain, so an oat is a grass.

clue.text: Units of resistance in people's 'ouses being reported?

indicators.note: being reported means we go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: 'ouses with a dropped H suggests Cockney speech, in which homes are 'omes

explanation.surface: Measuring electrical resistance in Cockney homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'ouses tells you to drop the H from the synonym too: homes becomes 'omes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Lavish old lover to get locked up, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the pieces are judged by how they sound

parts.words: old lover to get locked up
parts.note: an ex is a former partner; penned means shut in a pen, locked up

explanation.surface: A former partner, once generous, now sent to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, lavish means to spend or give freely, which is to expend.

clue.text: Make an effort leading smart meeting

indicators.note: leading puts the effort word at the front

parts.note: to try is to make an effort
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Trying hard to set up a stylish meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysting is the keeping of a tryst, a secret lovers' rendezvous or meeting.
